questions.stem: This patient developed the oral findings shown after starting chemotherapy. What underlying mechanism best explains why the oral mucosa is affected?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A direct chemical burn from the drug contacting the mouth

choices.label: C
choices.text: Autoimmune destruction of the salivary glands

choices.label: D
choices.text: A nutritional vitamin deficiency from poor oral intake

explanation.summary: Alkylating agents kill all rapidly dividing cells, including the oral and gastric mucosa, producing mucositis and ulceration; the injured mucosa and reduced flow give the thick, pasty saliva seen here.
explanation.whyCorrect: Alkylating agents kill all rapidly dividing cells, including the oral and gastric mucosa, producing mucositis and ulceration; the injured mucosa and reduced flow give the thick, pasty saliva seen here.

questions.stem: This chemical schematic shows mechlorethamine reacting with guanine bases located on adjacent DNA strands. What class of DNA lesion is being formed?

explanation.summary: Nitrogen mustards such as mechlorethamine are bifunctional and covalently bridge the N-7 of guanine on two opposing strands, producing an interstrand cross-link that blocks strand separation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Nitrogen mustards such as mechlorethamine are bifunctional and covalently bridge the N-7 of guanine on two opposing strands, producing an interstrand cross-link that blocks strand separation.

questions.stem: This figure links specific chemotherapy agents to their characteristic organ toxicities. Cyclophosphamide is mapped to the bladder; which urinary metabolite is directly responsible for that toxicity?

explanation.summary: Cyclophosphamide metabolism produces acrolein, which concentrates in the bladder and causes hemorrhagic cystitis; mesna binds and neutralizes acrolein to prevent this.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cyclophosphamide metabolism produces acrolein, which concentrates in the bladder and causes hemorrhagic cystitis; mesna binds and neutralizes acrolein to prevent this.

questions.stem: This illustration shows an alkylating agent modifying DNA across three sequential panels. What is the ultimate cellular consequence depicted by the fragmented strand in the final panel?

choices.label: B
choices.text: Enzymatic reversal of the alkyl adducts by a methyltransferase

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increased transcription of DNA repair genes

choices.label: D
choices.text: Restoration of normal complementary base pairing

choices.label: E
choices.text: DNA strand breakage that suppresses replication and triggers apoptosis

explanation.summary: Cross-linked DNA cannot separate for replication; the cross-linked strands eventually break and replication is suppressed, arresting the cell cycle and driving the cell to apoptosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cross-linked DNA cannot separate for replication; the cross-linked strands eventually break and replication is suppressed, arresting the cell cycle and driving the cell to apoptosis.
